## Course code and lab starters

Use this website as the primary source for course reading. To clone the code,
synthetic data, and lab starters, use the public GitHub repository:

<https://github.com/slzhao/BIOS6301-materials>

## Start here

1. Complete [Session 0](course/session00/index.qmd) before the first class.
2. Read the [course syllabus](syllabus.qmd).
3. Copy each lab starter from `course/` into the matching folder under `work/`.
4. Commit work before merging instructor updates.

## R dialect policy

Base R and tidyverse are both accepted. Some sessions target a specific tool for
learning, but otherwise choose the style that makes the data meaning and checks
easiest to audit. You should be able to read both and verify important results.

## Repository boundary

The repository has two ownership areas:

```text
course/    instructor-managed; read, render, and copy, but do not edit
work/      student-managed; create answers and commit your work here
```

Do not change anything under `course/`. Copy the relevant starter file or folder
from `course/` to the matching location under `work/` before editing it.

Before receiving course updates, save and commit work under `work/`. We will
practice this workflow in Session 2.

```bash
git status
git add work/
git commit -m "Save current work"
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/main
git push origin main
```

Do not place credentials, protected data, or restricted research data in either
directory.
